St. Procopius of Caesarea

Saints

St. Procopius of Caesarea

St. Great Martyr Procopius · St. Prokopios of Caesarea · Neanias, later Procopius

Period
Martyred in 303 in the cited OCA life
Region
Jerusalem; Caesarea in Palestine
Titles / vocation
Martyr
Commemoration
July 8

Introduction

A martyr of Caesarea during Diocletian’s persecution. His received life follows his transformation from imperial official to Christian confessor and his death by beheading.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomRemembranceChronology
Death / martyrdom

Beheaded at Caesarea, 303, according to the OCA life

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Originally called Neanius, he was from Jerusalem and entered imperial service. His father was Christian, while his mother initially remained pagan.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Opening paragraph

Life and notable events

The life recounts a vision of Christ and a radiant cross while he traveled toward Egypt. He later refused the emperor’s religious demands, endured imprisonment and torture, and received the name St. Procopius. The narrative also records the courage of twelve Christian women.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Conversion, arrest, imprisonment, and twelve women

Death and martyrdom

The OCA dates his martyrdom to 303 at Caesarea and describes his beheading with a sword after repeated tortures. Christians recovered and buried his body.

[1] Official Orthodox life · Concluding paragraph

Remembrance

The Greek Orthodox account likewise connects him with twelve women who suffered for Christ. This relationship identifies the Procopius named in the site’s historical explanation of the marriage service.

[2] Published Orthodox hagiography · Reading: imprisonment and twelve women

    Martyrdom at Caesarea in the OCA account.
